models.name: economic_forum_users
models.description:
Registered user accounts with email/password authentication credentials, email verification status, and profile information.

Stores primary identity information for authenticated users of the economic forum platform. Each user account is uniquely identified by email and secured with a hashed password. This table serves as the canonical source of user identity for the entire system, serving as the root of all ownership and permission relationships. User accounts are linked to their corresponding sessions through the economic_forum_user_sessions table and are referenced by economic_forum_user_email_verifications and economic_forum_user_password_resets for authentication workflows.

The designation of this table as an "actor" means it represents a true user type with its own distinct authentication flow, separate from any business domain entities like posts or attachments.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for login and communication. Must be a valid email format and globally unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Cryptographic hash of the user's password. Never store plain text passwords. Generated using bcrypt or similar secure algorithm.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this user account was created. Automatically set upon account registration and never modified.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this user account was last updated. Updated on any profile changes, password resets, or account status modifications.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this user account was soft-deleted. Nullable - if null, account is active. Used to preserve audit trail while hiding inactive accounts from user interfaces.

models.name: economic_forum_user_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for user authentication with access token, refresh token, and 24-hour expiration.

This table tracks login sessions for users of the economic_forum platform, serving as an append-only audit trail of authentication events. Each record represents a single user session established through successful login, containing connection metadata and temporal context necessary for security monitoring and session management.

Sessions are created upon successful authentication and expire after 24 hours by default. The system does not permit unlimited sessions for security reasons, so expired_at is always set.

This table has no independent API endpoints - all lifecycle operations are managed exclusively through the authentication subsystem.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: The user's {@link economic_forum_users.id} who owns this session.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The IP address used to establish this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL of the connection that established this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL that led to this session establishment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this session will expire. Always set to 24 hours after created_at. Not nullable to enforce security policy.

models.name: economic_forum_user_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens with 24-hour expiration to confirm user email addresses during registration before enabling file uploads.

This subsidiary table stores temporary one-time verification tokens issued during account registration or email change workflows. Each token is associated with a specific user and expires after exactly 24 hours for security. The presence of a record indicates the email address is unverified, while deletion (or expiration) signifies successful verification.

Tokens are designed to be single-use and cannot be reused. Users will receive the token via email and must enter it on the verification page to complete the process. The system uses this table to prevent unauthorized email changes and enforce reliable communication channels.

This table is managed entirely by the system during user registration and account modification flows, not through direct user CRUD operations - making it a subsidiary entity.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_user_id
foreignFields.description: User associated with this verification request. {@link economic_forum_users.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique one-time verification token generated for email confirmation. Must be cryptographically random and unguessable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was issued. Used to calculate 24-hour expiration window and enforce security policies.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token expires (24 hours after created_at). Must be exactly 24 hours after creation. Sessions cannot be extended beyond this point.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification record was soft-deleted (upon successful verification or manual cleanup). Absence indicates active/unverified status.

models.name: economic_forum_user_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for user account recovery with 1-hour expiration window.

Supports secure password recovery workflow by generating unique, time-limited tokens that users can use to reset their authentication credentials. Each token is associated with exactly one user account and becomes invalid after one hour from creation.

Tokens are used exclusively in the password reset workflow and are not exposed to users except via secure, encrypted communication channels. Once a password is successfully reset, the corresponding token is marked for deletion to maintain audit trail and prevent token reuse.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user account requesting password reset. {@link economic_forum_users.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique hashed token used for password reset validation. Generated securely and sent to user via email.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Exact datetime when the password reset token expires. Fixed 1-hour window from creation per security requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated and issued to the user.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was last modified (e.g. marked as used or deleted).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was logically deleted (soft delete). Used for audit trail tracking.

models.name: economic_forum_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email/password authentication credentials and elevated privileges for content moderation and user management.

Stores credentials and profile information for system administrators who have the authority to moderate content, delete inappropriate posts, and manage user accounts. This table serves as the canonical identity record for admin actors, with all authentication and session management flows centered around this entity.

Administrators are distinct from regular users because they have elevated permissions and are responsible for system integrity. Each admin has a unique email address for secure authentication and communication.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator email address for authentication and communication. Must be unique and used as the primary login identifier.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plain text. Used for secure login verification via bcrypt or equivalent hashing algorithm.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created. Records the initial registration date for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the administrator record. Updated whenever profile information is modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for administrator accounts. When set, the account is considered deactivated but retained for audit trails. Null value indicates active status.

models.name: economic_forum_admin_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for admin authentication with access and refresh token support for secure, persistent sessions.

Tracks login sessions for economic_forum_admins users with connection metadata including IP address, requested URL, and referrer information. This is an append-only audit trail that records each authentication event. Sessions expire after a defined period for security, and the expired_at field is mandatory to prevent unlimited sessions which pose security risks.

Each session is tied to exactly one admin account and cannot exist independently. The system uses this table to validate active sessions during requests and to audit login activity for security investigations.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The admin account associated with this session. {@link economic_forum_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The IP address from which the session was initiated. Required for security monitoring and geo-location tracking.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The full URL of the page that initiated the session. Used for tracking access patterns and identifying entry points.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL that led to this session initiation. Provides context about the source of the authentication request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this session was created. Required to establish session lifecycle and track duration.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this session will expire. Mandatory for security compliance to prevent unlimited sessions. Sessions must have an explicit expiration time.

models.name: economic_forum_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrative accounts with expiration and usage tracking.

Stores one-time tokens used to initiate password recovery workflows for economic_forum_admins. Each token is generated when an admin requests a password reset and is valid for a limited time. The system marks the token as used once it has been applied, rendering it invalid for future use.

Tokens are stored with explicit expiration dates and timestamps for security auditing. Soft deletion is supported to maintain a complete audit trail of all password reset attempts, including those that were never completed.

This table is managed entirely by the authentication system and not directly accessed or modified by end users.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin account requesting password reset. {@link economic_forum_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Randomly generated unique token string for password reset. Used to authenticate the reset request.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the password reset token. After this time, the token is no longer valid.

plainFields.name: used
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the password reset token has been successfully used to change the password.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was created and issued to the admin.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was last updated (typically when marked as used).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token record was soft-deleted. Null indicates the record is active. Used for audit trail preservation.

models.name: economic_forum_admin_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens to confirm admin email addresses during account registration or update.

Stores temporary tokens used to verify the authenticity of admin email addresses during account creation or email change procedures. Each token is unique, single-use, and expires after a defined period (typically 24 hours) to ensure security.

The token is sent to the admin's email address and must be presented to complete the verification process. Once verified, the token is invalidated. This table maintains an audit trail of all verification attempts, including successful validations and expired or unused tokens.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin account that this email verification is associated with. {@link economic_forum_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token generated for email confirmation. Must be cryptographically random and URL-safe to prevent guessing attacks.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the verification token. Tokens are always valid for a limited time (typically 24 hours) for security reasons.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was created and issued to the admin.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp indicating when this verification record was logically deleted, either upon successful verification or manual cleanup.

models.name: economic_forum_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings and feature flags governing the application's behavior.

Stores modifiable parameters that control forum functionality, such as feature toggles, display settings, rate limits, and system behaviors. Administrative users can enable or disable features through this centralized configuration system.

Each configuration key represents a specific behavioral control point that can be updated dynamically without code deployment. The active flag determines whether the configuration is currently applied to the running system.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key identifier. Must be a dot-separated hierarchical name (e.g., 'feature.upload.enabled'). All keys must be unique.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Configuration value stored as string. Can represent boolean, number, or text values encoded as string (e.g., "true", "5000", "default_template").

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and impact of this configuration setting.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this configuration is currently active and applied to the system. Inactive configurations are preserved for historical reference but ignored by the application.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was first created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this configuration.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was logically deleted. NULL means the configuration is still active (not deleted). Used for audit trail and recovery of configuration changes.

models.name: economic_forum_upload_limits
models.description:
System-wide file upload restrictions governing attachment size, type, and quantity limits for posts and comments.

Defines the technical constraints for all file uploads in the forum system, ensuring consistent policy enforcement across all user interactions. This configuration table establishes non-negotiable limits on file size, permitted MIME types, and the maximum number of files that can be attached to a single post.

These restrictions are applied globally to both post and comment attachments and are enforced by the application layer before any file upload processing occurs. The values in this table constitute the definitive policy for file upload operations and must be updated by administrators who have elevated privileges.

All attachments must comply with the declared constraints - any attempt to upload a file that exceeds the size limit, uses a disallowed extension, or exceeds the per-post limit will result in immediate rejection with a user-facing error message.

plainFields.name: max_file_size
plainFields.description: Maximum allowed file size in bytes for any single uploaded file. The system enforces a strict threshold of 5,242,880 bytes (5MB) to ensure performance and storage efficiency.

plainFields.name: allowed_file_types
plainFields.description: Comma-separated list of file extensions permitted for uploads. Must include: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .pdf, .txt, .docx, .csv. Any other file MIME types will be rejected at the application layer.

plainFields.name: max_files_per_post
plainFields.description: Maximum number of files that can be attached to a single post or comment. Limits the total count of attachment files per post to prevent abuse or performance degradation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this upload limit configuration was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this upload limit configuration. Tracks when administrators last revised the file upload restrictions.

models.name: economic_forum_moderation_flags
models.description:
Tracks moderation flags for posts triggered by three or more distinct user reports.

This subsidiary table records when a post has accumulated sufficient reports from distinct users to trigger automated moderation review. Each flag represents a single post that has reached the threshold requiring administrative attention. The table does not store individual report details but aggregates the count of distinct reporters.

This table exists purely to support the moderation workflow of posts and has no independent user operations. It's automatically created and managed by the system when report thresholds are met, and is referenced by moderation systems to identify posts needing review.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_post_id
foreignFields.description: The post that has been flagged for moderation. {@link economic_forum_posts.id}.

plainFields.name: report_count
plainFields.description: Total number of distinct users who have reported this post. When this reaches 3 or more, the moderation flag is activated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation flag was activated (i.e., when report_count reached threshold).

models.name: economic_forum_system_audits
models.description:
Audit log of all administrative actions including bans, post deletions, and moderation approvals.

Records immutable events when administrators perform system management actions. Each audit entry captures the actor who performed the action, the type of target entity affected, the specific action taken, and the reason provided.

This table is critical for accountability, legal compliance, and operational transparency. Audit entries are created once and never modified, ensuring data integrity of system actions.

Multiple actors (users and admins) can perform audits, so the actor_type discriminator field indicates whether the action came from a user or admin account. The target_type field identifies the entity type being modified (e.g., "post", "user", "comment").

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User who performed the audit action. {@link economic_forum_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who performed the audit action. {@link economic_forum_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the action. Values: "user" or "admin". Used to determine which actor table the foreign key references.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity that was affected by the audit action. Examples: "post", "comment", "user", "admin", "attachment". Used to identify the context of the action.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: ID of the entity that was affected by the audit action. References a record in another table (e.g., economic_forum_posts, economic_forum_users).

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: The specific administrative action performed. Values: "ban", "unban", "delete", "restore", "approve", "reject", "modify". Follows standard moderation action taxonomy.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation provided by the administrator for the action taken. Required for accountability and audit review.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit entry was created. This is immutable - the time the administrative action was performed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit entries. Required to maintain audit trail integrity without deleting records from the database.

models.name: economic_forum_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for users and administrators to confirm ownership of email addresses.

Records generated during user registration or email change workflows. Contains unique verification tokens with expiration time to ensure secure email confirmation.

System automatically generates these tokens and sends them via email. When a user clicks the verification link, the system validates the token and records the confirmation timestamp.

The token is invalidated after expiration or upon confirmation. Soft delete is supported to maintain audit trails while retaining the ability to identify invalid tokens.

Uses actor_type to differentiate between user and admin verification records, with corresponding foreign keys to economic_forum_users and economic_forum_admins.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_user_id
foreignFields.description: The user who requested email verification. {@link economic_forum_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The admin who requested email verification. {@link economic_forum_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor this verification record belongs to. Valid values: 'user' or 'admin'. Used to determine which actor table the foreign key references.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique random token generated for email verification. Used in verification link sent to user's email address. Must be encrypted in transit and at rest.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token was created and issued.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token expires. After this point, the token is invalidated and cannot be used for verification.

plainFields.name: confirmed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the email address was successfully verified by the user. NULL if verification is pending or failed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification record was soft-deleted. NULL means the record is active. Used to retain audit trail for revoked or expired tokens.

models.name: economic_forum_maintenance_modes
models.description:
Tracks whether the system is currently in maintenance mode and provides scheduling information for planned downtime.

This configuration table controls system-wide maintenance operations, determining whether users see a maintenance message instead of normal application content.

The maintenance mode is activated and managed by administrators through system controls, not by end users. It serves as a passive system control point that affects all users simultaneously.

When active, the application redirects users to a maintenance page instead of serving regular content.

This table does not track historical maintenance events - it only reflects the current or next scheduled maintenance state.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Indicates whether maintenance mode is currently active. True means the system displays a maintenance message instead of regular content.

plainFields.name: scheduled_start
plainFields.description: The scheduled start time for maintenance window. NULL means no upcoming scheduled maintenance.

plainFields.name: scheduled_end
plainFields.description: The scheduled end time for maintenance window. NULL means no upcoming scheduled maintenance.

plainFields.name: maintenance_message
plainFields.description: The message displayed to users when the system is in maintenance mode. Contains guidance about expected downtime and when service will resume.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this maintenance mode configuration was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this maintenance mode configuration was last updated.

models.name: economic_forum_posts
models.description:
User-created discussion posts with text content, moderation status, and chronological metadata.

Stores the primary content objects of the economic forum platform, representing questions, insights, or arguments posted by authenticated users. Each post can receive multiple replies in the form of comments and may be flagged or hidden through moderation workflows.

Posts are independently managed entities requiring full CRUD operations: users can create new posts, search across all posts, edit their own content, and delete posts they no longer wish to maintain. Administrators can flag or hide inappropriate content while preserving the audit trail.

The post remains attached to its original author even if author profile information changes, ensuring historical integrity of discussion context. Soft deletion is implemented to facilitate moderation policies while maintaining data integrity for audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_user_id
foreignFields.description: Author's user account. {@link economic_forum_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator who performed the last action (flag/hide). {@link economic_forum_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the post, limited to 200 characters for display clarity and search optimization.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content of the post in Markdown format. Contains the full text of the user's contribution, which may include formatting, links, and code blocks.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current moderation status of the post. Valid values: 'active', 'flagged', 'hidden'. Status transitions follow moderation workflow rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was originally created. Immutable and used for chronological ordering and feed generation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was last modified. Updated whenever title or body is edited by the author or administrator.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the post was soft-deleted. NULL indicates the post is active. Used for moderation workflows where posts are hidden rather than permanently removed.

models.name: economic_forum_post_comments
models.description:
Threaded comments and replies to posts, supporting up to 5 levels of nesting with parent-child relationships.

Stores user-generated replies to forum posts with hierarchical structure, allowing users to respond directly to specific comments or posts. Each comment is associated with a single post and created by an authenticated user through their session.

Comments have a nested structure where replies can be posted to other comments, forming parent-child relationships up to five levels deep. This enables threaded discussions while maintaining performance through proper indexing.

Comments are soft-deletable for moderation purposes and tracked with full audit trail via created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at timestamps. Users can edit their own comments within a reasonable time window, with updates reflected in the updated_at field.

Each comment is tied to exactly one post through post_id and one user through user_id, ensuring proper ownership and attribution. File attachments are managed separately in the Attachments component via economic_forum_post_attachments junction table.

foreignFields.name: post_id
foreignFields.description: The forum post this comment belongs to. {@link economic_forum_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: The parent comment this is a reply to. Self-referential relationship. {@link economic_forum_post_comments.id}.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: The authenticated user who created this comment. {@link economic_forum_users.id}.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: The text content of the comment. Contains the user's reply or response.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this comment was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this comment was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this comment was soft-deleted for moderation purposes. If null, comment is active.

models.name: economic_forum_post_reports
models.description:
User-submitted reports on forum posts for moderation review.

Records reports made by authenticated users against specific posts. Each report contains a reason provided by the reporter and a status that tracks the moderation workflow (pending, reviewed, resolved, or rejected). Reports are independent entities with their own lifecycle and can be searched, filtered, and acted upon by moderators regardless of the associated post.

Reports are linked to the reporter through economic_forum_users and to the reported post through economic_forum_posts. When a post is deleted, its reports remain in the system for audit purposes. Soft deletion is supported to preserve historical data while allowing moderators to clean up obsolete reports.

foreignFields.name: reporter_id
foreignFields.description: Reporter user's {@link economic_forum_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: reported_post_id
foreignFields.description: Reported post's {@link economic_forum_posts.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the user for reporting this post. Maximum 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current moderation status of the report. Valid values: 'pending', 'reviewed', 'resolved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report was last updated (e.g., when status changed).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report was soft-deleted. If null, the report is active.

models.name: economic_forum_attachment_files
models.description:
Stores file metadata for uploaded attachments including unique hashed filename, original filename, MIME type, file size, and upload timestamp.

Contains immutable metadata for files attached to posts, ensuring file integrity, tracking, and efficient retrieval. Each record represents a single uploaded file with its technical properties, used by the application to serve files and validate uploads. The actual file storage is managed externally (e.g., cloud storage), with this table storing only reference and metadata information.

Files are linked to posts via the economic_forum_post_attachments junction table. This table exists purely as supporting metadata and is not independently managed by users - attachments are created and deleted via their parent posts.

plainFields.name: hashed_filename
plainFields.description: Unique hashed filename generated to prevent storage conflicts and enable secure file referencing. Uses secure hashing algorithm to create unique identifier from original filename and content.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: The original filename as provided by the user during upload. Preserved for display purposes and to maintain user intent, but never used for file storage or direct access.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: The official MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Used for content delivery and validation to ensure only permitted file types are uploaded.

plainFields.name: size
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes. Enforces maximum 5MB (5,242,880 bytes) limit per file as specified in requirements. Stored as double to accommodate precise byte counting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded and metadata was recorded. Used for sorting attachments in upload order within posts and for audit purposes.

models.name: economic_forum_post_attachments
models.description:
Junction table linking posts to their attached files, ensuring each attachment is associated with exactly one post and maintaining order of upload.

This table manages the many-to-many relationship between economic_forum_posts and economic_forum_attachment_files by creating a direct association with an explicit sequence number. Each attachment record in this table points to one specific post and one specific file, establishing the parent-child relationship between content and media.

The sequence field (integer) determines the display order of attachments under each post, with lower numbers appearing first. This ensures attachments are presented in the exact order they were uploaded by the user.

This junction table enables efficient querying of all attachments for a given post while maintaining the upload sequence, and prevents direct interaction with attachments outside the context of their parent post.

When a post is deleted, all associated attachment records in this table are automatically removed as a cascading deletion through the foreign key relationship.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_post_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the post that this attachment belongs to. {@link economic_forum_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_forum_attachment_file_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the file record containing metadata for this attachment. {@link economic_forum_attachment_files.id}.

plainFields.name: sequence
plainFields.description: Numeric order of attachment within the post. Lower values appear first, ensuring attachments are displayed in upload sequence. Must be positive integer.
